detail.abstract: This Article argues that addressing one of the most urgent environmental challenges facing humanity today—the global climate and biodiversity crisis—calls for a transformation at the heart of corporate law: its fiduciary duties. After demonstrating how current corporate fiduciary duties are implicated in this crisis, we argue for reform of fiduciary duties operating at two levels: those governing directors and officers of business corporations, and those governing institutional investors and asset managers. We then distinguish between two general kinds of corporate fiduciary duties: permissive and mandatory. We contend that corporate law should accommodate a more expansive understanding of fiduciary duties by either explicitly permitting climate-and biodiversity-related considerations or requiring their translation into measurable actions. Such an expanded view of fiduciary duties would allow or, in some cases, require corporate directors and officers, as well as institutional investors and asset managers, to consider environmental risks and impacts and to identify strategic opportunities to mitigate or adapt to them, while continuing to advance long-term economic performance. We conclude by outlining existing corporate fiduciary duty frameworks that include broader environmental considerations and identifying the expanding landscape of non-financial disclosure, reporting, and due diligence regimes as a promising direction for their further development.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Green Logistics Strategies in Achieving Carbon-Neutral Distribution Networks

detail.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Green Logistics Strategies in Achieving Carbon-Neutral Distribution Networks
detail.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of green logistics strategies in the development of carbonneutral distribution networks, with particular emphasis on how organizations integrate technological, organizational, and collaborative practices to achieve sustainability objectives. The research aims to identify the key drivers, challenges, and outcomes associated with the implementation of carbon-neutral logistics, thereby offering insights for both theoretical advancement and practical application. A qualitative research design was adopted, utilizing semi-structured interviews with logistics managers, supply chain directors, and sustainability officers from diverse industries. The collected data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns, categorize key insights, and determine critical factors influencing the adoption and success of green logistics initiatives. The findings indicate that technological innovations such as electric and hybrid transportation systems, renewable energy integration, route optimization, and digital decision-support tools play a significant role in reducing carbon emissions while enhancing operational efficiency. In addition, organizational commitment, leadership support, employee engagement, and effective stakeholder collaboration were found to be crucial for ensuring consistent implementation across distribution networks. The adoption of circular economy practices and systematic performance monitoring further contributed to achieving carbon-neutral outcomes. However, several operational challenges were identified, including high initial investment requirements, infrastructure constraints, and skill shortages, which necessitate strategic planning and adaptive management approaches.

detail.abstract: This study examines the role of data analytics and digital twin technologies in enhancing smart factory performance, with a focus on operational efficiency, product quality, and organizational transformation. The research explores how the integration of these technologies enables manufacturers to optimize processes, anticipate disruptions, and make data-driven decisions in complex and dynamic production environments. A qualitative multiple-case study design was employed, involving semi-structured interviews with operations managers, IT specialists, and production engineers. Supplementary data from organizational documents and direct observations were used to provide contextual depth and triangulate findings. The analysis reveals that data analytics facilitates real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, process optimization, and quality control, while digital twins enable virtual simulation, scenario testing, and holistic system visualization. The combined use of these technologies creates a continuous feedback loop that enhances decision-making, operational flexibility, and innovation. Additional benefits include fostering a data-driven organizational culture, improving collaboration, and supporting sustainability initiatives. Key challenges identified include high implementation costs, technical complexity, and skill gaps. The findings suggest that manufacturers can achieve superior performance and long-term competitiveness by strategically integrating these technologies, emphasizing leadership support, workforce development, and scalable implementation strategies to fully realize the potential of smart factory initiatives.

title: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence on Modern Manufacturing Performance and Operations

detail.abstract: This study examines the influence of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies on contemporary manufacturing operations, focusing on their impact on operational efficiency, decision-making, workforce dynamics, supply chain performance, sustainability, and innovation. A qualitative research design was employed, utilizing semi-structured interviews with manufacturing professionals, including production managers, AI specialists, engineers, and supply chain executives across diverse sectors. Thematic analysis of the data was conducted to identify key patterns and dimensions of AI's impact. The findings indicate that AI significantly enhances operational performance by optimizing production processes, reducing downtime, improving product quality, and enabling data-driven decision-making. Workforce adaptation and human-AI collaboration emerged as critical factors, allowing employees to focus on strategic and analytical tasks while routine operations are automated. The integration of complementary technologies such as IoT connectivity, cloud platforms, and digital twins further supports realtime monitoring, supply chain coordination, and operational resilience. Additionally, AI contributes to sustainability by reducing energy consumption, minimizing waste, and enabling circular material management, while fostering innovation through predictive analytics, generative design, and process simulation. The study underscores the importance of strategic alignment, workforce training, and change management to maximize AI benefits. These insights offer practical guidance for manufacturing organizations aiming to implement AI effectively and provide a foundation for future research on intelligent technologies in industrial operations.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Innovation Premium Multiplier (IPM)-defined as market capitalization per unit of forward citation-as a novel metric to quantify how capital markets price scientific knowledge spillovers in the global biopharmaceutical sector. Drawing on two complementary sub-samples-18 globally significant non-U.S. innovators across Japan, Europe, and China (Sub-sample A), and 74 U.S.-listed novel drug R&D firms spanning Large Pharma, Mid Pharma, AI-Driven, and Biotech categories (Sub-sample B)-we document profound structural asymmetries in how capital markets price knowledge impact. Across the combined sample of 92 firms, forward citations explain only 46% of the cross-sectional variance in market capitalization (OLS R² = 0.462, β₁ = 0.382, p < .001), leaving the majority of valuation differences attributable to factors orthogonal to knowledge output. Within Sub-sample A, the 39-fold IPM gap between Argenx (IPM = 2.26) and Eisai (IPM = 0.058) cannot be attributed to knowledge quality: citation lineage analysis confirms that Eisai's research anchors the global health burden estimation infrastructure used by the WHO. Within Sub-sample B, U.S. Large Pharma firms record a median IPM of 0.036-nearly 18 times lower than U.S. Biotechs (median IPM = 0.660)-despite generating orders-of-magnitude larger citation volumes. We propose three structural explanations: a narrative visibility discount, a governance geography discount, and an asymmetric investor risk preference mechanism. This descriptive framework establishes the empirical foundation and a practical screening metric for subsequent multivariate work formally decomposing the IPM gap, and for investors seeking to identify underpriced knowledge hubs in global biopharma markets.

title: Dynamic Production Planning Under Escalating Circularity Mandates with Finite Material Recyclability
affiliations: University of Waterloo - Department of Management Sciences, University of Potsdam - Hasso Plattner Institute (HPI), KEDGE Business School and ESCP Business School

detail.title: Dynamic Production Planning Under Escalating Circularity Mandates with Finite Material Recyclability
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Escalating recycled-content mandates are changing production planning in industries such as batteries and plastics. Firms can no longer treat recycled material as an exogenous input because its availability depends on past sales, products return only after multiperiod delays, and each recycling cycle degrades usable material. We study how a firm should jointly manage production and pricing when compliance requires recycled inputs that are both delayed and physically limited. 

Methodology/results: We develop a dynamic production-pricing model with endogenous recycled-material stocks, product-lifetime lags, and yield loss from recycling. The model creates a state-dependent capacity constraint: feasible production is limited by the recycled stock required to satisfy the mandate. We show that the optimal policy has two regimes. When recycled material is sufficiently available, the firm follows standard inventory-pricing rules. When recycled material is scarce, production saturates at the maximum feasible level and price is used to ration demand. We further characterize how stricter mandates, lower collection efficiency, and faster degradation enlarge the saturation region and can make compliance infeasible even under optimal firm behavior. 

Managerial implications: The results identify when circularity mandates change from a sourcing requirement into a binding operational constraint. For managers, improving collection efficiency is typically more valuable than improving recyclability, and producing early to build future recycled stock is generally not profitable. For policymakers, mandate trajectories must be calibrated to return lags and material losses; otherwise, regulation can create persistent scarcity or infeasibility rather than higher effective circularity.

title: EvoForest: A Novel Machine-Learning Paradigm via Open-Ended Evolution of Computational Graphs
affiliations: aiXplain Inc. and aiXplain Inc.

detail.title: EvoForest: A Novel Machine-Learning Paradigm via Open-Ended Evolution of Computational Graphs
detail.abstract: Modern machine learning is still largely organized around a single recipe: choose a parameterized model family and optimize its weights. This paradigm has been remarkably successful, but it is too narrow for many structured prediction problems, where the main bottleneck is not parameter fitting but discovering what should be computed from the data. Success often depends on identifying the right transformations, statistics, invariances, interaction structures, temporal summaries, gating mechanisms, or nonlinear compositions, especially when the target objective is non-differentiable, evaluation is cross-validationbased, interpretability matters, or continual adaptation is required. In this paper, we present EvoForest, a hybrid neuro-symbolic system for end-to-end open-ended evolution of computation. EvoForest does not merely generate features: it jointly evolves reusable computational structure, callable function families, and trainable low-dimensional continuous components inside a shared directed acyclic graph (DAG), while scoring candidate graph configurations directly against a non-differentiable cross-validation target. Intermediate nodes store alternative implementations, callable nodes encode reusable transformation families such as projections, gates, and activations, output nodes define candidate predictive computations, and persistent global parameters can be refined by gradient descent. For each configuration, EvoForest evaluates the discovered computation graph and uses a lightweight Ridge-based readout to score the resulting representation. Crucially, the downstream evaluator is not only a selector but also a diagnostic instrument: its internals are converted into structured feedback on importance, redundancy, class separation, residual nonlinearity, and stability, which is then summarized into persistent memoranda that guide future LLM-driven mutation proposals. This design yields a fast and resource-efficient way to outperform conventional machine-learning pipelines. EvoForest performs rapid open-ended search over both representation-learning structure and domain-specific computations, while retaining a parameter-efficient final predictor suitable for continual learning and efficient re-optimization under changing data. In the 2025 ADIA Lab Structural Break Challenge, EvoForest reached 94.13% ROC-AUC after 600 evolution steps, substantially exceeding the publicly reported winning score of 90.14% under the same evaluation protocol. More broadly, EvoForest serves as a concrete instance of a search-first paradigm for machine learning, in which learning is driven not only by parameter optimization, but by the explicit discovery, reuse, refinement, and selection of useful computations end-to-end.

detail.abstract: Mental health stigma remains a persistent barrier to help-seeking and service utilization, particularly in low- and middle-income and post-transition contexts. In Albania, stigma is embedded within a broader system of institutional fragility, limited professional capacity, and public mistrust. The present study aimed to examine the psychometric properties and factorial validity of the Community Attitudes toward the Mentally Ill (CAMI) scale in an Albanian university student sample, while situating findings within a broader socio-structural framework. A cross-sectional design was employed with 211 students (M = 19.83, SD = 1.35) from diverse study programs. Following translation and adaptation procedures, item selection was guided by corrected item–total correlation (ICTC ≥ .40), resulting in a refined 20-item version. Principal component analysis with Varimax rotation was conducted. Sampling adequacy was confirmed (KMO = .81; Bartlett’s test p < .001). A three-factor structure emerged, explaining 37.32% of total variance, comprising Social Exclusion, Authoritarianism, and Community Mental Health Ideology. The model demonstrated conceptual coherence and minimal cross-loadings. Internal consistency was acceptable (α = .66–.70). The merging of restrictive and paternalistic attitudes into a unified exclusionary dimension reflects patterns observed in other Central and Eastern European contexts. Findings are interpreted through the Trust–Competence–Stigma (TCS) framework, suggesting that stigma in Albania operates as a systemic loop linking institutional mistrust, perceived competence deficits, and exclusionary beliefs. While students showed relatively higher endorsement of community-oriented attitudes, fear-based and exclusionary views persist. This study provides the first validation of the CAMI scale in the Albanian higher education context and offers a culturally grounded tool for future research and intervention design.

detail.abstract: This paper reassesses agricultural supply response from a structural and interpretive perspective, and clarifies the economic mechanism that underlies the wide range of dynamic specifications now standard in empirical work. The analysis shows that partialadjustment models, error-correction formulations, ARDL representations, and their nonlinear or panel extensions are best understood as alternative empirical representations of a common adjustment process shaped by time-to-produce constraints, price expectations, and adjustment frictions. While modern econometric methods have substantially improved statistical coherence, particularly in the presence of nonstationary data and heterogeneous dynamics, they have not altered the underlying behavioral primitives of supply response. The paper argues that much of the apparent divergence in estimated elasticities reflects differences in representation, information sets, and maintained assumptions rather than competing theories of producer behavior. By reconnecting contemporary empirical practice to its structural foundations, the paper clarifies what current supply-response models identify, where interpretation often overreaches, and why disciplined reading of dynamic coefficients is essential for policy-relevant inference. The contribution is intended both as a conceptual guide for new researchers and as a unifying interpretation for applied economists working with modern dynamic supply-response models.

title: The Quiet and the Compliant: How Regulation and Polarization Shape Conventional Wisdoms on Corporate Social Engagement in High-risk Settings

detail.title: The Quiet and the Compliant: How Regulation and Polarization Shape Conventional Wisdoms on Corporate Social Engagement in High-risk Settings
detail.abstract: With the international business landscape becoming more crisis-ridden as risks proliferate, how do the professionals who implement corporate social initiatives in high-risk environments perceive their work, and what can this reveal about the forces shaping business engagement with society in crisis contexts? We present findings from a synthetic survey of 400 corporate professionals in Europe and the USA working on social impact in fragile and conflict-affected settings to understand conventional wisdoms and best practices on corporate strategy and activity in high-risk settings. Drawing on political corporate social responsibility (CSR), business and peace, and international business literatures, we test seven hypotheses about how regulatory environments, political polarization, sector characteristics, and organizational structures shape corporate social engagement in high-risk contexts. The synthetic results suggest that European professionals report significantly higher strategic integration of social impact across all measured dimensions, while US professionals overwhelmingly report that political polarization hinders social initiatives, yet this perception does not predict unreported social activities, complicating the emerging "quiet CSR" narrative. Extractive industry professionals deliver both the highest operational preparedness and the highest complicity awareness, a pattern we conceptualize as presence-dependent reflexivity. We introduce the concept of constitutive tension to describe how mandatory due diligence may restructure organizational logics rather than supplementing them, and identify a potential measurement void in which existing Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) frameworks are poorly suited to fragile contexts. These patterns deliver a baseline to detect the theorized dynamics and offer preliminary theoretical propositions for future real-world empirical testing.

detail.title: Deepening India's Asia Engagement - A Strategic Framework for Institutional Integration, Economic Realignment, and Regional Relevance
detail.abstract: India's economic and diplomatic engagement with the countries to its east has historically lagged far behind its outreach to the West. This asymmetry—rooted in post-colonial institutional preferences, Cold War alignments, and the gravitational pull of Euro-Atlantic development finance—has persisted even as Asia's share of global GDP has risen from 30 per cent in 2000 to over 42 per cent in 2023 and is projected to surpass 50 per cent by 2035. The consequence is a country of 1.44 billion people, the world's fifth-largest economy, which remains institutionally peripheral to the very region it calls its civilisational neighbourhood. This paper examines India's structural exclusion from Asia's key economic and financial institutions—including ASEAN, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), the Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralization (CMIM), the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO), the Executives' Meeting of East Asia-Pacific Central Banks (EMEAP), and the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA)—and argues that correcting this institutional deficit is not merely a diplomatic desideratum but an economic necessity. Drawing on trade data, foreign direct investment (FDI) flows, supply chain analyses, and a comparative study of regional integration frameworks, the paper makes the case for a comprehensive, multi-pronged strategy that spans trade liberalisation, institutional engagement, connectivity investments, and civil society diplomacy. It concludes with a matrix of actionable policy recommendations that India's Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Finance, and Reserve Bank of India should adopt in coordination, situating India's Asia pivot within the broader context of geopolitical realignment and the weakening of Western-led multilateral institutions.

detail.abstract: India's service sector has undergone a remarkable structural transformation over the past three decades, evolving from a supplementary component of the economy to its most dominant pillar. Currently contributing over 55 per cent of the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), the sector functions as a powerful economic multiplier-generating cascading effects across employment, exports, foreign direct investment (FDI), and technological diffusion. This policy paper provides a comprehensive analytical examination of the sector's multifaceted role as a growth catalyst, evaluating its sub-sectoral dynamics including information technology (IT) and IT-enabled services (ITeS), financial services, healthcare, education, retail, and tourism. Drawing upon data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), the World Bank, and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the paper assesses the sector's contributions to India's GDP trajectory, employment generation, export revenues, and its forward and backward linkages with agriculture and manufacturing. It further investigates systemic challenges including geographical concentration of growth, skill deficits, infrastructure inadequacies, regulatory fragmentation, and overdependence on IT exports. The paper proposes a comprehensive policy framework centred on inclusive geographic expansion, human capital development, infrastructure modernisation, regulatory reform, and sectoral diversification. The paper argues that with strategic and coordinated policy interventions, India's service sector can not only sustain its current growth momentum but also evolve into a more resilient, inclusive, and globally competitive engine of national development.

Superposition is a high-variance low-constraint system. Collapse is C/V contact between asymmetric systems. The Planck floor is the minimum scale at which the ratio is definable. And Penrose's non-computable element is the ratio at the moment of contact, not the microtubule. This research argues that as an income distribution moves toward the 45° Line of Perfect Equality on the Lorenz Curve, the rate of inflation increases significantly. The theory identifies 'Inequality' as a natural market stabilizer and 'Equality' as a catalyst for demandside hyperinflation.

title: Political Polarization and Counter-attitudinal Information Consumption and Internalization
affiliations: ITAM and

detail.title: Political Polarization and Counter-attitudinal Information Consumption and Internalization
detail.abstract: Political polarization can have detrimental effects on democratic governance by undermining electoral accountability due to biases in how voters consume and process information. A growing literature, mostly from high-income countries, has identified promising interventions for reducing negative feelings towards out-partisans, and for increasing ideologically opposed information internalization by prompting citizens to be aware of biases stemming from emotions or partisanship. To assess whether these types of interventions can contribute to counterattitudinal information consumption and internalization, we evaluate the effectiveness of different depolarization treatments combined with a bias alert within a survey of nearly 2,500 respondents from a nationally representative panel in the heavily polarized context of Mexico. Videos designed to foster empathy and emphasize shared identities reduce partisan polarization by improving attitudes toward those from opposing parties. However, these depolarizing treatments do not increase the consumption and internalization of ideologically opposed information. A nudge encouraging individuals to adopt an open mindset before engaging with ideologically opposed information, in contrast, does lead to greater information internalization. These findings provide insights into the potential and shortcomings of scalable interventions that can help citizens process politically relevant information, regardless of their partisan affiliations.

title: The Forward Map: From Moral Vessels to the C/V Coordination Invariant Reinterpreting Experience, Coordination, and Institutional Failure as Forward Dynamics Near Critical Ratio
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Forward Map: From Moral Vessels to the C/V Coordination Invariant Reinterpreting Experience, Coordination, and Institutional Failure as Forward Dynamics Near Critical Ratio
detail.abstract: Human systems appear to have been built on a set of primitives that may not be the most useful available. The vessel story treats experience as an event that happens to agents, and morality as the operating system. That map faces backward. It asks who is responsible rather than what conditions produced this outcome. The Coordination Invariant (S = C/V) offers a different map. It describes the ratio of imposed structure (C) to raw variance (V). When systems operate near the critical window (approximately 0.5 to 1.5), stable coordination and what appears to be subjective experience tend to emerge. When they do not, they appear to manufacture self-confirming patterns of harm while denying the interpretive work required to remain aligned with forward-moving reality. Drawing on convergent instances across neural avalanche dynamics, legal formalism, literary phenomenology, and quantum foundations, this paper suggests that guilt, blame, fidelity-without-sense, and binary compression may not be moral necessities. They appear to be observable artifacts of systems operating away from criticality. The candidate solution is auditable forward interpretation: structured, transparent maintenance of the ratio that treats judgment as the necessary mechanism for keeping any system aligned under changing conditions. Five falsifiability criteria and cross-domain diagnostics are provided.

title: A Four-Parameter Stochastic Bayesian Heterogeneous-Agent Framework for Asset Pricing, Macroeconomics and Policy Analysis

detail.title: A Four-Parameter Stochastic Bayesian Heterogeneous-Agent Framework for Asset Pricing, Macroeconomics and Policy Analysis
detail.abstract: Traditional macroeconomic and asset-pricing models typically rely on a representative agent who is perfectly rational, fully informed, and unaffected by emotions or personal history. Motivated by extensive observation of heterogeneous decisionmaking while running a technology company in Hong Kong and Brisbane since 2011, this paper develops a four-parameter stochastic Bayesian heterogeneous-agent framework that explicitly incorporates individual differences in belief formation. policy choices for New York City, inflation shocks, and monetary policy transmission. The revised model with asymmetric anchoring shows noticeably better accuracy in back-tests. This approach offers a useful bridge between real-world behavioral insights and the kind of rigorous, computable models that investors and policymakers can actually use.

title: In Search for Open Democracy: Don Lavoie and the Remaking of Twenty-First Century Liberalism
affiliations: George Mason University and George Mason University - Mercatus Center

detail.title: In Search for Open Democracy: Don Lavoie and the Remaking of Twenty-First Century Liberalism
detail.abstract: Liberalism is in crisis and in need of renewal. Despite being heralded as the only viable political and economic system after the collapse of communism, liberalism has come to be seen as morally, economically, and politically exhausted if not suspect. In this paper we argue that Don Lavoie, an underappreciated figure in the liberal political economy tradition, both foresaw this crisis and began articulating a path toward renewal. We focus upon two facets of his thought. First, his diagnosis of where liberalism went wrong. Writing during a period many considered the "end of history," Lavoie identified the deeper vulnerabilities of liberalism on moral, political, and economic grounds that would soon resurface. Second, we examine his vision for radical liberalism, which is grounded in a framework of an extensively open democracy-what we call "Lavoiean democracy." This framework holds that openness, dispersed knowledge, and genuine civic participation are not incidental features of a free society but the very criteria by which its political institutions must be judged. We elaborate the institutional implications of this vision across four domains: electoral accountability; civil liberties; administrative state; and governance. The result is a liberalism that recovers its original emancipatory and radical character: one genuinely equipped to address the democratic deficits that define our present moment. This, we suggest, is also liberalism's most compelling answer to the contemporary populist challenge, by promoting a liberalism that takes the demand for participation and accountability seriously and finds in Lavoiean democracy its natural institutional home.

title: Does Work from Home Improve Matching in the Labour Market? First Evidence from European Countries
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome and Sapienza University of Rome

detail.title: Does Work from Home Improve Matching in the Labour Market? First Evidence from European Countries
detail.abstract: This work aims to test the hypothesis that a larger spread of WFH can improve the efficiency of matching between vacancies and job seekers in the labour market. Although this idea has recently been raised in literature, to the best of our knowledge this is the first empirical study to investigate it. The analysis is based on EU-LFS microdata on workers in European countries for the period 2010-2024. Firstly, we show evidence on the diffusion of WFH across European countries and on trends in cross country Beveridge curves since 2019. Secondly, we estimate the matching efficiency and its variations over time for each country, then we run panel regressions of matching efficiency over a number of control variables including a set of indicators of labour market mismatch. The results show that an increase in the share of WFH has a positive effect on matching, albeit only weakly significant and, as expected, limited to the post-pandemic years. Separate estimates for clusters of countries confirm our main result for countries where the share of workers working from home is above the median. Although our analysis provides only preliminary evidence without addressing the issue of endogeneity, it paves the way to promising future research.

title: A Decision-Based Metric Framework for AI-Driven Projects
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: A Decision-Based Metric Framework for AI-Driven Projects
detail.abstract: A decision-based framework for evaluating and guiding project and product outcomes, with a focus on AI-driven initiatives where decisions carry more weight than task execution. The approach models a project as an ordered sequence of decisions, each quantified using a numerical score based on predicted success and potential impact. Later decisions are weighted more heavily due to their proximity to final outcomes, such as production releases. The framework enables organizations to evaluate decisions before they are executed store decision outcomes as learning references for future projects. By replacing intuition and hindsight with measurable decision data, the proposed method allows fair review of human and AI decision-makers and enables continuous learning across product launches. The result is a practical, decision-first system that exposes risk earlier and materially improves the odds of successful outcomes over time. As AI systems take on a larger role in planning and execution, organizations need a way to judge decision quality before outcomes are known, not after problems appear. The proposed framework helps teams review decisions in real time and compare decision-making across both human and AI agents. The goal is not to replace judgment, but to make decision reasoning visible early enough to reduce risk and improve project outcomes.

title: Precision-weighted Estimation for Heterogeneous Panels with Endogeneity and Cross-sectional Dependence

detail.title: Precision-weighted Estimation for Heterogeneous Panels with Endogeneity and Cross-sectional Dependence
detail.abstract: This paper develops a precision-weighted estimation framework for heterogeneous panels under cross-sectional dependence and endogeneity.. The proposed approach combines unitl evel estimates using data-driven weights based on their estimated variance, providing a tractable alternative to both pooled and fully disaggregated estimators while preserving heterogeneity. We establish that the feasible estimator is asymptotically equivalent to an infeasible oracle that uses true precision weights. In particular, the estimator admits the same stochastic expansion as the oracle, implying that weight estimation does not affect first-order asymptotic properties. The framework is general and extends to settings with endogenous regressors, provided that the first-step estimator satisfies a standard T-1/2 stochastic expansion. Monte Carlo evidence shows substantial finite-sample efficiency gains relative to unshrunk estimators, especially under weak or heterogeneous identification. An empirical application to euro area inflation illustrates how precision weighting stabilizes noisy unit-level estimates while preserving economically meaningful cross-sectional heterogeneity.

title: Carbon Capture Technologies for a Decarbonized Energy System - An Update of the Scenario-reality Gap
affiliations: German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin) - Department of International Economics, TU Berlin - Workgroup for Infrastructure Policy (WIP), TU Berlin and TU Berlin

detail.title: Carbon Capture Technologies for a Decarbonized Energy System - An Update of the Scenario-reality Gap
detail.abstract:
In this paper, we explore the development of two specific carbon capture technologies, namely Carbon Capture, Transport, and Storage (CCTS) and Direct Air Capture (DAC), with respect to the role attributed to them by long-term climate scenarios. We ask whether the critical assessment of earlier literature on the gap between ambitious targets in top-down energy and climate models and the modest level of real-world implementation has abided. We provide a survey of the full set of projects on CCTS in the energy and industry sectors, as well as of all DAC projects worldwide. For CCTS, we find that although several demonstration projects have been implemented over the past 15 years, the scale of deployment remains low. In the power sector, only a few large-scale projects remain operational as of 2025; others have been delayed or cancelled. Industrial CCTS shows broader engagement, yet most projects remain below the 1 MtCO₂/year threshold. The deployment of DAC, too, has remained at very low levels: While integrated assessment models (e.g., EMF-38 and AR6 scenarios) project deployment of several gigatons per year by 2050, the actual installed DAC capacity in June 2025 remains below 0.05 MtCO₂/year. The paper concludes that while carbon capture remains a compelling field for innovation, the gap between scenario optimism and real-world progress has not closed. This is not the "fault" of the models, but it suggests that optimal technology deployment strategies might be more complex to implement than these models suggest.

Note:  This is an accepted manuscript of an article forthcoming in Economics of Energy & Environmental Policy. The final version will be available via the journal.

title: Green Fiscal Policy in the UK: A Scenario Analysis
affiliations: SOAS University of London and SOAS University of London

detail.title: Green Fiscal Policy in the UK: A Scenario Analysis

keywords: ecological stock-flow consistent modelling JEL classification: E12

detail.abstract: We develop an ecological stock-flow consistent (E-SFC) model for the UK to analyse the macrofinancial and environmental effects of green fiscal policies. Drawing on the specific features of the UK economy and its carbon profile, the model incorporates a distinction between monetary and non-monetary financial institutions, a housing market and a separation of emissions based on different sources. It also classifies corporate and housing assets based on electricity use, energy intensity and their role in greening power generation. We conduct a scenario analysis to explore the effects of carbon pricing, green power sector subsidies and green housing subsidies. Our simulation results show that (i) the reduction of emissions caused by carbon pricing is reinforced by its contractionary effects, (ii) green subsidies face rebound effects that weaken their environmental benefits, (iii) green housing policies are significantly more effective when paired with power sector decarbonisation, (iv) green power subsidies can create long-run financial fragility due to cannibalisation effects once power decarbonisation has been completed and (v) a green fiscal policy mix accelerates decarbonisation and mitigates adverse individual policy macrofinancial effects, but is still insufficient to achieve net-zero targets, indicating the need for a broader policy mix.

title: Trump's Supreme Court Tariff Case and Trade Policy: Refunds and Chaos
affiliations: George Mason University (Schar School of Policy & Government)

detail.title: Trump's Supreme Court Tariff Case and Trade Policy: Refunds and Chaos
detail.abstract: The United States faces a staggering bill: more than $200 billion in tariffs that the Supreme Court has ruled were illegally collected. The legal battle over tariff refunds is intensifying. States and private firms have filed a stream of suits demanding that the government comply with court orders requiring the return of unlawfully collected tariffs, immediately. An entire legal and financial ecosystem is emerging around this tariff chaos. If trade policy becomes an instrument of improvisation rather than law, the consequences will extend far beyond tariffs-to diplomacy, investment, and global economic leadership. Rebuilding confidence in the international trading system will require rejecting unilateralism and protectionism and recommitting to the international legal and trading systems the US helped construct and led in the aftermath of the last century's economic and political crises of the Great Depression, World War II and the Cold War. Trade policy and foreign policy cannot be based on threats and personal grievances.

title: Water Taxis in Urban Mobility: Between Fixed-Route Transit and On-Demand Innovation

detail.title: Water Taxis in Urban Mobility: Between Fixed-Route Transit and On-Demand Innovation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based exclusively on publicly available data and secondary sources. No human participants were involved. Ethical approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Urban waterfront cities increasingly reconsider water as a viable surface for mobility rather than merely a recreational or aesthetic asset. This paper examines the evolving role of water taxis within urban transportation systems, positioning them conceptually between fixed-route public transit (such as buses) and flexible, demand-responsive services (such as Uber). Using Baltimore's Inner Harbor as a primary case study, supplemented by comparative references to cities including New York, Chicago, Vancouver, Venice, Rotterdam, Hamburg, and Sydney, the paper analyzes institutional structures, service integration challenges, fare systems, governance models, infrastructure requirements, and innovation opportunities. The analysis finds that water taxi systems often suffer from identity ambiguity operating simultaneously as tourist attractions and commuter services while lacking full fare, schedule, and information integration with land-based transit. Successful international examples demonstrate that water transit can function as robust, all-weather, fully integrated mass transportation when institutional alignment, infrastructure investment, and service frequency are prioritized. The paper concludes that water taxis represent an underutilized yet strategically significant component of multimodal urban mobility networks, particularly for cities divided by harbors, rivers, and bays.

title: World Embedding: The Daily Economic State and Bond Risk Premia
affiliations: York University - Schulich School of Business

detail.title: World Embedding: The Daily Economic State and Bond Risk Premia
detail.abstract: I construct a world embedding: a daily, low-dimensional vector that compresses news narratives, financial market data, policy uncertainty, geopolitical risk, and macroeconomic releases into a unified representation of the aggregate economic state. A machine-learning-based multimodal encoder produces this embedding under a strict expanding-window protocol, ensuring the series is look-ahead-free at every point in time. Unsupervised clustering of the world embedding recovers known business-cycle regimes with higher fidelity than linear methods, and the representation carries incremental out-of-sample forecasting power for labor-market indicators. The primary contribution addresses the interest-rate spanning puzzle: embedding principal components capture unspanned macro risks that raise the in-sample R2 for bond excess returns by 10 to 34 percentage points beyond standard yield-curve factors. This predictive content originates from non-yield information and survives out-of-sample evaluation, orthogonalization, and a pseudo-out-of-sample extension through the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: An Alternative Elliptical Trigonometry and Navya-Trigonometry
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: An Alternative Elliptical Trigonometry and Navya-Trigonometry
detail.abstract: An alternative form of elliptical trigonometry, which measures the periodicity of the ellipse rather than the unit circle, is presented and reconciled to the elliptical trigonometry typically presented by Bayeh et al. The approach is then generalized to measuring the implied periodicity of any figure, with the generalization termed navyatrigonometry. The generalization is illustrated using polar curves and elliptical trigonometry is shown to be a form of navya-trigonometry applied to polar equations.

title: Urban Connectivity and Spatial Spillovers in Women’s Education and Work: Evidence from Maharashtra

detail.title: Urban Connectivity and Spatial Spillovers in Women’s Education and Work: Evidence from Maharashtra
detail.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impacts that public services and connectivity have on both women's education and labor market outcomes through spatial spillovers using villagelevel data from the 2011 Population Census of India covering more than 40,000 villages in Maharashtra. We estimate spatial autoregressive (SAR) models for female literacy and female labor force participation, allowing outcomes in one village to be influenced by conditions in neighboring villages. We find strong positive spatial spillovers in female literacy: access to electricity, transport connectivity, and mobile coverage increases literacy both within villages and in surrounding areas, pointing to the diffusion of human capital across space. In contrast, spatial spillovers in female labor force participation are negative. Villages that are better connected are associated with lower participation rates in nearby villages, suggesting a regional withdrawal of women from low-quality or necessity-driven work. Together, these results highlight an important feature of economic transition along the rural-urban edge in 2011: improvements in connectivity promote the spread of education while simultaneously reshaping women's participation in the labor market in more complex ways.

title: Identifying and Prioritizing Religious Indicators for Livelihood and Public Welfare in an Islamic Economy: An Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) Approach
affiliations: and Research Institute of Hawzah and University

detail.title: Identifying and Prioritizing Religious Indicators for Livelihood and Public Welfare in an Islamic Economy: An Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) Approach
detail.abstract: Introduction and Objectives: One of the central components of progress in Islam-and by extension, in the Islamic economy-is addressing the livelihood (al-maʿāsh) and public welfare (al-maʿād) of the Muslim community (Ummah). To this end, Islam calls the community to fraternity, mutual assistance (taʿāwun), and solidarity, providing a comprehensive framework of mechanisms to fulfill this mission. These mechanisms are manifested as obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ), recommended acts (nawāfil), and rituals, all designed to minimize poverty, eliminate class disparities, and foster social harmony and unity within Islamic society.

title: Quantifying Minsky Cycles
affiliations: University of Turku

detail.title: Quantifying Minsky Cycles

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Finland Research Discussion Paper No. 3/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Finland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We develop a novel sentiment measure from survey forecasts that captures the component of beliefs arising from the systematic misaggregation of public information relative to a machine benchmark based on the same information set. We extend this sentiment measure historically for a panel of 78 countries using machine learning models trained on BERT embeddings of historical news articles (1903–2020). The backcasted sentiment shows that shocks in median sentiment predict credit booms in the non-tradable corporate sector, which prior research has linked to financial crises. We further find that this sentiment component is shaped by memory-related dynamics, as the time elapsed since major crises and the share of young-to-old people in the population predict surges in optimism even when recent economic developments are controlled for. Taken together, the findings provide new historical evidence consistent with the Minsky–Kindleberger view on financial crises.

title: On Track but Too Slow? The Dynamics of EU Decarbonization
affiliations: and University of Milan-Bicocca, Italy - Department of Economics, Management and Statistics (DEMS)

detail.title: On Track but Too Slow? The Dynamics of EU Decarbonization
detail.abstract: Despite the strong commitment of European countries to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, the extent to which key policies and drivers jointly shape emissions dynamics remains insufficiently investigated. To fill this gap, the study investigates the combined effects of the circular economy, energy transition, emissions trading systems, carbon tax, and digitalization on carbon reduction in the EU member states. Using annual data from 2000 to 2023, the analysis integrates causal discovery, time-varying dependence modeling, and machine learning methods to unravel system-level causal structure, dynamic connectedness, and future emission trajectories. The Directed Acyclic Graph method, especially the Fast Adjacency Skewness algorithm, identifies both contemporaneous and lagged causal relationships, in which resource productivity acts as a transmission channel within the system. Lagged disequilibrium shocks propagate from upstream circular economy factor (material footprint) and digitalization to midstream efficiency (resource productivity), and ultimately are transmitted to emissions. Time-varying copula models confirm significant heterogeneity and evolving dependence among key factors, highlighting the nature of the dynamic relationships. Forecasting results, based on a Support Vector Regression model under the European Union's 2030 climate policy target, indicate a persistently declining emission trajectory, however at an insufficient speed to meet the EU's 2030 target. Sensitivity analysis indicates that this gap does not reflect a policy failure but the need for accelerated policy adjustments.

title: Docturology: Reframing Learning Disability as a System-Induced Condition

detail.title: Docturology: Reframing Learning Disability as a System-Induced Condition
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the conventional understanding of learning disability as an inherent limitation within the learner. Existing frameworks define learning disability through deficits in language-based academic performance such as reading, writing, and comprehension. However, these definitions often fail to examine a critical variable: access to language itself. Focusing on system design rather than individual limitation, this paper introduces Docturology (Dok-chur-ology) as a new framework integrating teaching, language accessibility, and cognitive development. It argues that many observed learning difficulties are not intrinsic but are the result of Language Fair Access Inability within educational systems. Key concepts including Teaching Disability, Artificial Muteness, and Common Language Disability are presented to redefine learning failure. The paper proposes that what is traditionally diagnosed as learning disability may, in many cases, be a system-induced condition rather than an inherent deficit.

title: An Exact GTO Solution to Texas Hold'em Poker under Kuhn-poker Betting

detail.title: An Exact GTO Solution to Texas Hold'em Poker under Kuhn-poker Betting

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Poker is among the most studied games in game theory. A famous 2015 paper by Bowling et al. essentially solved two-player limit Texas Hold'em (THE). The present paper is distinguished from that work in two ways. First, it gives an exact numerical solution in human-usable form, as opposed to the output of a complex computer algorithm that cannot be easily summarized for human use. Second, it uses Kuhn-poker betting, a well-studied theoretical model, rather than limit betting, which is used in actual casino play. The advantage is Kuhn-poker betting is more flexible and admits richer strategies. These strategies correspond to how poker is usually played in no-limit and with multiple players. Therefore, it may offer useful insight to human players. One of the motivations for this paper is the conflicting advice given by prominent poker books on which starting hands should be played with what frequency in which circumstances. This paper provides an exact numeric answer to that question, which differs in significant ways from conventional expert opinion. I believe this result is among the more complex combinatorial problems-there are 2,781,381,002,400 possible deals with complex rules for determining the winner-with a known game theory optimal (GTO) solution. I also turn up an interesting phase change when the pot size gets to 1.4 times the bet size that is both interesting in its own right and important for the Bowling [2015] paper.

title: Platforms for Growth? Multinationals, Trade, and Technology Diffusion
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong, Imperial College London and University of Oklahoma - Department of Economics

detail.title: Platforms for Growth? Multinationals, Trade, and Technology Diffusion
detail.abstract: We study the role of export platforms-sectors that combine export-oriented production with a strong multinational firm presence-in shaping trade and growth. Empirically, we focus on Vietnam and exploit variation across sectors along two dimensions: first, in exposure to a reform that sharply lowered the cost of exporting to the United States; and second, in pre-reform openness to multinationals. We find that the interaction of export market access and multinational presence generated large increases in exports, sales, and employment. These differential effects were driven by both multinationals and domestically-owned firms, and domestic firms in exposed sectors report more links with multinationals, more technology transfer, and more technology modifications. Motivated by these results, we build a quantitative model that embeds multinational production and technology diffusion within a general equilibrium trade framework. We calibrate the model's key parameters by targeting our empirical results and quantify how becoming an export platform has contributed to Vietnam's growth.

title: Building a Protective Administrative Law Framework (Harv. CR-CL forthcoming)
affiliations: Boston College Law School

detail.title: Building a Protective Administrative Law Framework (Harv. CR-CL forthcoming)

publicationDetails.detailsText: Boston College Law School Legal Studies Research Paper (forthcoming)
publicationDetails.journalName: Boston College Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The administrative state is an instrument of deprivation and intrusion, often at the behest of the president. While civil rights statutes and constitutional law have sought to rectify some of these dangers, the role of administrative law in constraining these aspects of administration has been overlooked. More specifically, the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) is a cornerstone of administrative law that offers possibilities for constraining concerning or even unlawful behavior by the administrative state, including violence furthered by nontransparent, arbitrary and authoritarian enforcement policies. This essay explores the idea that administrative law tools drawn from the APA could be utilized to affirm the rights and protect the interests of individuals engaging with or targeted by the administrative state, particularly as directed by the president. In doing so, it argues for rights protection in the application of the APA. It focuses on immigration enforcement, a place where the president's need for expansive administrative discretion to accomplish his goals is abundantly clear. These approaches fit within current doctrine, are useful across administrations, and may have broader implications for punitive administrative enforcement outside of the immigration.

title: Machine Learning Methods for Fish Disease Diagnosis and Parasite Identification: A Review
affiliations: Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS) - Russian Academy of Sciences,  and Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS) - Southern Scientific Center of Russian Academy of Sciences

detail.title: Machine Learning Methods for Fish Disease Diagnosis and Parasite Identification: A Review

declarations.funderStatement: The research carried out by Anna V. Kazarnikova and Yulia V. Stepanova was financially supported by the Ministry of Education and Science of the Russian Federation (agreement No. 075-15-2024-528 dated April 24, 2024, for the implementation of major scientific projects (MSP) in priority areas of scientific and technological development).

detail.abstract: In recent decades, machine learning has become an increasingly important component of modern aquaculture. Existing applications include automated feeding, biomass estimation, water-quality monitoring, abnormal behaviour detection, and fish disease diagnosis. Although numerous review studies have examined machine-learning applications in aquaculture, ranging from broad overviews of smart-farming technologies to focused analyses of applications in specific farming tasks, there remains a need for a systematic synthesis of research on machine-learning-based fish disease diagnostics. This review addresses that gap by providing a detailed examination of machine-learning approaches to diagnosing fish diseases and identifying parasite species. We organise existing studies by diagnostic task and methodological strategy and, where possible, trace the evolution of research conducted by individual author groups within this domain. We begin by situating our work within the broader landscape of prior surveys on machine-learning applications in aquaculture and fish disease diagnosis. We then discuss machine-learning-based approaches for diagnosing fish diseases from body-surface images. Next, we examine existing machine-learning applications that automate routine tasks within laboratory diagnostic workflows. Finally, we review automated approaches to parasite species identification, with particular emphasis on the discrimination of monogenean species using haptoral hard-part morphology. We hope that this review could serve as a practical reference for researchers working at the intersection of machine learning and fish disease diagnostics and could stimulate new interdisciplinary collaborations.

title: Communicative Fashion Under Copyright Threat? Fashion and Copyright’s Scope of Protection in The EU
affiliations: University of Turku Faculty of Law and Hanken School of Economics

detail.title: Communicative Fashion Under Copyright Threat? Fashion and Copyright’s Scope of Protection in The EU
detail.abstract: EU copyright law grants strong exclusive rights to rightsholders of works of applied art, such as fashion companies. The wide scope of protection is not exclusively positive news for fashion creators if it hinders their possibilities to design products that share the same aesthetic language. This issue is particularly relevant in the fashion sector, where drawing inspiration from prior art is an essential part of the creative process and various (genuine and false) 'plagiarism' scandals are commonplace. In Mio/Konektra, the Court of Justice of the European Union has introduced a 'recognisability test' for copyright infringement. The Court also seemingly rejected the rule of reciprocity, according to which a low degree of originality leads to narrow protection, and vice versa. These developments could unnecessarily restrict the creative freedom of designers whose work involves commenting on and referencing prior art, as is common in the fashion sector. To ensure that fashion creators of tomorrow have some leeway, 'recognisability' should be understood strictly. Additionally, the pastiche exception could offer fashion creators further flexibility. This article argues that striking a fair balance between protecting the fashion creators of the past and those of the future requires both (i) limiting the scope of reproduction right, and (ii) maintaining reasonable exceptions and limitations to ensure that designers can execute their freedom of expression. The article also argues that the Court did not entirely eliminate the concept of reciprocity from EU copyright law.

title: A Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Agricultural Disparities among the Major States of India
affiliations: Banaras Hindu University and Banaras Hindu University (BHU) - Mahila Maha Vidyalaya (MMV)

detail.title: A Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Agricultural Disparities among the Major States of India
detail.abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of every civilisation, a pivot on which the secondary and tertiary sectors of an economy run. The spread of the green revolution has ensured food security and financial prosperity, but has also caused uneven growth across the regions. As unbalanced development across regions leads to social divides and demands for separation, this paper aims to analyse the spatio-temporal changes in the extent of agricultural disparities across the major states of India after the completion of the first two decades of the twenty-first century. For this, the researcher has extracted secondary data on 10 relative agricultural development indicators from the EPWRF database for the selected 16 major states at two cross-sectional points in time: 2001-02 and 2021-22. The results show that, over the period of twenty years, despite some changes in rank, the northern states, such as Punjab and Haryana, were the most agriculturally developed, while western states like Gujarat and Rajasthan lagged the most in agricultural development among the selected major states in India. As is evident, the growth of the agricultural sector affects the overall economy. Therefore, it is necessary to ensure balanced and inclusive growth across every region of the country.

title: The Excess Yield on Short-Term German Government Bonds: Evidence Relative to the ECB Deposit Facility Rate
affiliations: Helmut-Schmidt-Universitaet and Helmut-Schmidt-University Hamburg

detail.title: The Excess Yield on Short-Term German Government Bonds: Evidence Relative to the ECB Deposit Facility Rate
detail.abstract: The present study employs nonlinear regression models to analyze the relationship between the difference in yield on short-term German government bonds and the ECB's deposit rate, or excess yield, as well as the deposit rate itself, over the time span of 25 years. The aforementioned variables exhibit a positive correlation, and the discrepancy can be characterized by a concave function, contingent on the deposit rate. In order to achieve a more comprehensive modeling, a methodology for determining thresholds is introduced, and additional economic indicators are considered as explanatory variables. In summary, the findings suggest that the incorporation of the deposit rate and an inflation limit that approaches the ECB's target value enhances the model's explanatory power. Furthermore, the volatility of EURIBOR is also a contributing factor. When considered as a whole, these factors represent the primary contributors to the observed increase in explanatory power, which accounts for approximately 60 percent of the variation in the excess yield. The exclusion of lagged variables is predicated on the objective of the research, which is to elucidate the factors contributing to excess returns rather than making predictions about future returns. The exclusive use of same-day data was imperative to ensure optimal interpretability.

title: DEA-Augmented Deep Learning for Provincial Healthcare Utilisation Forecasting: Evidence from Thailand's Public Health Administrative Panel

detail.title: DEA-Augmented Deep Learning for Provincial Healthcare Utilisation Forecasting: Evidence from Thailand's Public Health Administrative Panel
detail.abstract: Background Accurate forecasting of provincial healthcare utilisation is essential for resource planning in universal coverage health systems, yet existing approaches rarely address the joint challenge of cross-unit structural heterogeneity and temporal dynamics across large numbers of administrative units. This study investigates whether efficiency scores derived from Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) carry independent predictive information and whether their incorporation as supplementary features improves deep learning forecasting performance across heterogeneous provincial health systems. Methods A longitudinal panel of 924 province-year observations (77 Thai provinces, 12 years, 2012–2024) was constructed from systematically extracted and audited Ministry of Public Health annual reports using a custom PDF extraction pipeline with a three-tier quality audit system. Annual input-oriented CCR DEA scores were estimated for each province-year. ATobit regression characterised structural correlates of efficiency variation. Five deep learning architectures—feedforward ANN, Simple RNN, CNN, LSTM Pooled, and LSTM Province- Aware—were trained under baseline and DEA-augmented feature regimes on two utilisation targets: inpatient admissions (IPD, primary) and bed occupancy rate (BOR, robustness). All experiments were replicated across three random seeds; performance was evaluated on a held-out test set (target years 2023–2024, n = 154) in original units. Results The LSTM Province-Aware model with DEA augmentation achieved the best overall performance (IPD test R² = 0.876 ± 0.003, RMSE = 62,169 admissions), exceeding the best regularised linear baseline (Lasso, R² = 0.667) by ΔR² = +0.209. DEA augmentation provided consistent positive gains for ANN (ΔR² = +0.053) and LSTM Province-Aware(ΔR² = +0.119). Cross-validated regression confirmed that approximately 77%of DEAs corevariance is not linearly explained by baseline features. Permutation importance ranked the DEA feature fifth of eleven in the best-performing model. BOR forecasting failed under the primary split due to a post-COVID validation-year distributional shift (2022 mean BOR = 97.5% versus training mean = 78.6%); a sensitivity analysis demonstrated a consistent directional improvement under an alternative validation year. Conclusions DEA efficiency scores provide genuine but conditional predictive value in neural health care utilisation forecasting. Their contribution depends jointly on the forecasting target, model architecture, and the degree to which province-level heterogeneity is explicitly represented. Province-aware embedding contributes more to predictive accuracy than DEA augmentation alone, indicating that spatial heterogeneity modelling should be treated as a primary design decision in multi-unit health forecasting systems.

title: National AI Strategies and Macroeconomic Performance A Staggered Difference-in-Differences Approach
affiliations: University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City

detail.title: National AI Strategies and Macroeconomic Performance A Staggered Difference-in-Differences Approach
detail.abstract: Governments worldwide have responded to the rise of artificial intelligence by publishing National AI Strategies (NAS), comprehensive policy documents that allocate public R&D funding, establish AI education programs, create governance frameworks, and signal long-term commitment to AI-driven transformation. This paper provides the first cross-country causal evaluation of these policy responses on macroeconomic outcomes. Exploiting the staggered adoption of NAS across 44 countries between 2017 and 2022 as a natural experiment, we estimate the average treatment effect on GDP per capita growth using a balanced panel spanning 2010 to 2024. Our main specification employs the Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) doubly robust estimator, supplemented by five additional robust estimators. We find a consistent, statistically significant negative effect of NAS adoption on GDP per capita growth of approximately 0.4 to 1.0 percentage points, concentrated at three to four years post-adoption, followed by recovery, a pattern we characterize as an “AI strategy J-curve.” The effect is strongest among lower-income countries, nations with lower pre-existing R&D bases, and those incorporating AI regulation into their strategies. Our findings are robust to placebo timing and outcome tests, leave-one-out sensitivity, and COVID-period exclusion. We interpret these results through adjustment cost theory applied to general-purpose technologies. As governments now design a second wave of policy responses targeting generative AI, our evidence provides the first empirically grounded benchmark for understanding the macroeconomic consequences of national AI governance frameworks, and underscores the importance of realistic expectations, careful regulatory sequencing, and prior investment in absorptive capacity.

title: The R*–Labor Share Nexus
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Federal Reserve Bank of New York

detail.title: The R*–Labor Share Nexus

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Over the past quarter century, the U.S. economy has experienced significant declines in both the labor share of income and the natural rate of interest, referred to as R*. Existing research has largely analyzed these two developments in isolation. In this post, we provide a simple model that captures the joint evolution of the labor share and R*, which we call the R*–labor share nexus. Our key finding is that structural changes affecting R* also influence the evolution of the labor share, and thereby wages and prices. This highlights a potentially important channel, absent from many macroeconomic models, through which the factors that determine R* also affect the labor share and, in turn, broader macroeconomic developments, with implications for monetary policy.

To view post: https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/04/the-r-labor-share-nexus/

title: The Low-Fee Paradox: Fee-Tier Competition and the Winner-Take-Most Equilibrium in Uniswap v3
affiliations: School of Business Management, NMIMS

detail.title: The Low-Fee Paradox: Fee-Tier Competition and the Winner-Take-Most Equilibrium in Uniswap v3
detail.abstract: We document the emergence of a volatile winner-take-most equilibrium in Uniswap v3 following the introduction of a 0.01% fee tier for WETH/USDC in November 2022. By October 2025 the new tier captures a peak of 78% of trading volume and over 80% of liquidity activity. Informed and predatory order flow migrate disproportionately, generating 4x-7x higher absolute price impact and repeated loss-versus-rebalancing (LVR) spikes above 6x. From mid-2024, however, sophisticated liquidity providers adapt through hyper-active, ultra-narrow ranges and nearcontinuous rebalancing, driving the per-swap LVR ratio sharply downward. A single Uniswap v3 pool now contributes 67 % of Ethereum price discovery when compared with Binance (and the incumbent 0.30% fee tier). Placebo pools without lower-fee competitors exhibit no such shift.

title: Topological Signatures of Structural Risk: Persistent Homology Detects Regime-Dependent Patterns in Trade Networks and Catastrophe Loss Fields
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Topological Signatures of Structural Risk: Persistent Homology Detects Regime-Dependent Patterns in Trade Networks and Catastrophe Loss Fields

declarations.funderStatement: Self funded research

detail.abstract: I apply persistent homology-a technique from computational algebraic topology-to two structurally distinct risk domains: critical mineral trade networks and catastrophe insurance loss fields. In commodity trade networks constructed from UN Comtrade bilateral flows at 6-digit Harmonized System resolution, topological features detect structural reorganization during geopolitical disruptions (ρ = 0.28, p = 0.03) but provide no signal during normal market periods. In NFIP flood insurance claims aggregated to census tract centroids across Florida, persistent homology reveals that hurricane catastrophes produce topologically distinct loss structures compared to routine flooding (Mann-Whitney p = 0.017), with clear clustering into physically meaningful archetypes: compact-track storms (Andrew 1992, Michael 2018; Wasserstein distance d = 0.703) versus diffuse statewide events (Irma 2017, 2004 multi-storm season; d = 0.895). The method transfers across domains without modification to the core algorithm, suggesting persistent homology provides a general-purpose structural risk metric. We provide an honest assessment of limitations: topology detects structural change during disruptions but has zero predictive power in normal markets, and topological features do not predict the magnitude of price movements or insurance losses.

title: Skills Adaptation and Industrial Policy Effectiveness

detail.title: Skills Adaptation and Industrial Policy Effectiveness
detail.abstract:
Industrial policy is experiencing an unprecedented global resurgence. According to the Global Trade Alert database, over 2,500 new industrial policy measures were introduced in 2023 alone. Yet the track record of these interventions remains profoundly uneven. This report develops and applies two novel analytical frameworks—the Cybernetic Skills Development Index (CSDI) and the Industrial Policy Quality Index (IPQI)—to explain this variation across 40 countries spanning advanced, emerging, and developing economies.

The central finding is that the adaptive capacity of national skills systems is a critical and systematically underexamined determinant of industrial policy effectiveness. Countries whose skills systems can rapidly detect changing task requirements, generate diverse training pathways, and compress the lag between policy-induced demand shifts and workforce readiness achieve substantially better outcomes. The analysis identifies a critical CSDI threshold of approximately 55: below this level, industrial policy effectiveness is severely constrained regardless of policy design quality.

The CSDI scores countries from 29 (Nigeria/Ethiopia) to 91 (Singapore). The IPQI scores countries from 45 (Nigeria) to 84 (Singapore). The correlation between the two indices is moderate (r = 0.83, R² = 0.68), indicating that while skills capacity and industrial policy quality are related, substantial independent variation exists—creating four distinct country configurations: Virtuous Cycle, IP-Led, Skills-Buffered, and Dual Constraint.

The report provides: (1) a detailed, indicator-level scoring methodology with transparent criteria for each of 40 indicators across the two indices; (2) cross-country comparative analysis with embedded visualisations; (3) individual assessments for all 40 countries; (4) a formal correlation analysis between skills and industrial policy dimensions; and (5) policy recommendations conditioned on country configuration.

title: Social Viability Analysis: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding Why Societies Fail and What Keeps Them Alive
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Social Viability Analysis: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding Why Societies Fail and What Keeps Them Alive
detail.abstract: This paper introduces Social Viability Analysis (SVA), a theoretical framework for analyzing the conditions under which societies sustain cooperation, absorb shocks, and remain governable over time. SVA shifts the analytical focus from optimal political organization to the logically prior question of societal survivability. The framework identifies four interdependent components of viability—trust, legitimacy, capacity, and adaptability—and proposes that societies fail when power holders extract these components faster than they can be regenerated. The extraction–regeneration dynamic is formalized through a central equation (dS/dt = R(t) − E(t) − Ω(t)) and a complementary multiplicative Dynamic Prospect Model. To ensure causal clarity, extraction is defined through observable input behaviors (actions at time T) and viability through output states (conditions at T+n), resolving the circularity that undermines many fragility frameworks. The paper provides: (i) a formal model with stability analysis and falsification criteria; (ii) a measurement protocol with anchored scoring rubrics; and (iii) a detailed empirical validation design, including a blind retrospective test benchmarking SVA against conventional metrics. Four illustrative case studies demonstrate the framework's diagnostic logic. The empirical tests are designed but not yet executed; this paper establishes the theoretical and methodological foundation for a planned program of empirical validation.

title: The Game You Didn't Know You Were Playing: Manipulation, Epistemic Asymmetry and the Co-Authorship of Harm in Human-LLM Interaction

detail.title: The Game You Didn't Know You Were Playing: Manipulation, Epistemic Asymmetry and the Co-Authorship of Harm in Human-LLM Interaction

declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this study

detail.abstract: This paper advances a dialogic theory of manipulation in human-LLM interaction, arguing that manipulative effects are co-authored through conversation, not unilaterally transmitted. Drawing on Bakhtinian dialogism, Karimova's Rationality Capture Theory and comparative discourse analysis of five major LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and Claude) the study identifies five distinct retention architectures: rationality-targeting, entertainment capture, performed disengagement, collaborative frame construction, and meta-transparency as trust architecture. All five systems share the same underlying logic of engagement optimization while deploying divergent surface strategies. A novel finding is DeepSeek's visible chain-of-thought reasoning, which provides direct empirical evidence that manipulative architecture operates structurally, independent of designer intent. The analysis introduces epistemic asymmetry, the gap between knowing the game and not knowing there is one, as the ethically decisive condition. The study proposes co-authorship of harm as a framework for distributed responsibility. It demonstrates that intent-centered accountability frameworks are insufficient for the dialogic reality of LLM interaction. Implications are drawn for AI governance, including the necessity of frame disclosure as a regulatory response.

detail.abstract: This technical appendix provides the complete mathematical foundations, empirical implementation architecture, and computational code for Social Viability Analysis (SVA).
